cameras.name: microscopic_imager
cameras.reference_pose_note: Fixed stowed-arm visualization pose. MarsLab derives the virtual pinhole from the MI optics-box front face; original extended NASA calibration pose is retained in calibration_reference_pose. Not flight-calibrated stowed extrinsics.
cameras.rendering_fidelity: Pinhole approximation with geometry-derived stowed mount. NASA intrinsics remain cited; physical entrance pupil, dust-cover transmission, close-focus microscope response, radial distortion and detector response are not reproduced.

calibration_reference_pose.reference_pose_note: Calibration reference arm pose; not stowed. Retarget using CAHVOR_POS/QUAT for a different arm pose.

pose_source.author: MarsLab
pose_source.method: Visualization-derived virtual pinhole at center of MI optics-box front face; view direction is outward face normal; image up follows turret local +Z.
pose_source.status: Approximate visualization mounting proxy, not NASA flight-calibrated stowed extrinsics. The mesh has no separately resolved entrance pupil; physical dust-cover transmission and microscope focus are not modeled.
pose_source.shared_model_note: Spirit and Opportunity share this source stowed arm geometry, so their mounting proxy is identical; their individual NASA optical calibration metadata remain distinct.

components: mossbauer target beneath panels, also usable by APXS
science_instruments.name: Calibration Targets

engineering_sensors.mount: inside rover, explicitly not rover center of mass
engineering_sensors.notes: Source describes EDL telemetry averaging; avoid asserting 8 Hz is mandatory surface simulation rate.

engineering_sensors.quantity_note: One per six independently driven wheels; count follows described six-wheel mechanism.

physical.mass_discrepancy_note: PDS original host description gives 180 kg, NASA Spirit overview and JPL flight-system telecom description give 185 kg. Preserve citation and selection instead of presenting the choice as uniquely exact.
physical.geometry_note: PDS says dimensions at wheelbase, not explicit axle-center coordinates; do not silently equate width with tire-center track. Calibrated mesh/joint locations should govern controller wheel coordinates.
physical.inertia_policy: Published total mass and sparse instrument masses constrain an explicitly labeled engineering approximation. Geometry-derived primitive or mesh inertia is computed, not a NASA flight tensor. Do not claim NASA certifies inferred link distribution.
physical.frame_note: PDS native MER frame +X forward toward PMA, +Z down, +Y completes right hand (right). Navigation origin directly above middle wheels; mechanical origin 0.29 m forward. Convert explicitly into simulation +Z up.

coordinate_frame.source: MER Rover Navigation; X forward, Y right, Z down, origin above middle wheels
coordinate_frame.translation_status: Nominal ground clearance 0.29 m (JPL surface mobility paper §2.1) plus NAIF structures-SPK definition of NAV origin at bottom panel between middle wheels. Nominal dimensions, not a per-rover flight survey.

limitations: No public source reviewed provides all flight link masses/inertias; any analytic partition is explicitly a MarsLab engineering approximation.
No lidar fitted. No GPS receiver fitted.
Spectrometer/environment/housekeeping interfaces do not claim physical sensor emulation.
Historical original complement, excluding later hardware failures.
MER Nav-origin ground height uses published nominal body clearance, not a millimetre-accurate flight survey.
MI runtime mounting is a MarsLab geometry-derived proxy matched to the fixed stowed arm mesh; source NASA reference pose is preserved separately.

navcam_left.limitation: Rendering-only near clipping bypasses opaque lens/camera-housing surfaces in the NASA visualization mesh while preserving calibrated optical centers and orientations. Objects inside the near plane cannot be rendered. This is not a measured flight optical near limit. Full calibrated lens distortion and detector response are not simulated.
